What was equally pleasing for Jim in winning this his first Championship was beating fellow clubmate Simon Holmes, who with David Harvey was running in this one as a guest.

Simon Holmes led the lads home, with 23rd place in 15m. 08s. Backing up Simon were:- 40th, Dave Harvey (15m. 43s.); 66th, Len Hobbs (16m. 45s.); 67th Reg Hopkins (16m. 46s.); John Cambridge 84th in 18m. 09s.; and Tony Holmes, who clocked 20m. 34s.
In the Boys race, our first man home was Simon Holmes, seventh in 14m. 38s., while Jimmy McAffie was 11th in 14m. 51s., Reg Hopkins, 21st in 15m. 58s., and John Cambridge 21st in 16m. 53s.

Simon Holmes made it a Belgrave one-two finishing second in 2m55.7s. We are so used to seeing Martin Bloice first past the post that we were a little disappointed to see him finish 4th in the Junior 300m in 38.0s.
He only needs to record a somewhat faster time. Fourth place in the intermediate 1,500m. went to Simon Holmes in 4m. 19s., while Dave Raffell was fourth in the intermediate shot.
In the youths' events, Dave Harvey and Simon Holmes had good middle-distance wins, and weren't afraid to try their hand at field events either.

John Martin, at his strongest ever having reached mid-way in his winter's weight training schedule, blasted the shot beyond anyone else's reach and another to show he was in fine fettle was Simon Holmes, racing to a 16 second victory in the 2 miles having started with all but three of the 28 strong field ahead of him.

Simon Holmes was going well but most of our other men seemed to find the heavy course difficult to negotiate. By six miles Simon, who had placed 10th for University College in the London Colleges League race three days earlier, was closing right up on Pat and on the last lap pulled away from him for a very fine run.

Once again Simon Holmes led the rest home and our team position at the end of the day was 60th. Pretty poor you might think, although due respect must be shown to those who ran, but looking around it can be seen that the malady from which we are suffering is not confined to the Bels.

Simon Holmes, the revelation of the winter season, added Jim Rimmer's scalp to his growing collection with a 'P.B.', and others to record their best times were Peter Hardwick and junior Pete Gardner who is maturing steadily into a most reliable runner.

Simon Holmes ran well under 2 minutes for the 800 metres yet again - what a good summer he has had - and Cliff Brooks notched up another big individual score of 23 points.
